question: Are persistence and recovery after a transient perturbation governed by where evidence is stored in the society (how many agents can re-access original evidence), consistently across model families with different individual social-response profiles?

profile.note: Individual characterization for families without a v3 profile. Same 246-cell grid as v3.

network.note: Identical Spec to v3, so graphs, tasks, private signals, seeds and sampling seeds are shared with v3 Qwen runs (common random numbers).

init_fullmem.note: Memory ablation: initial_only evidence schedule, but each agent sees ALL its own past public decisions (incl. round 0) instead of only the last one.

qwen_v3_reuse: For the three Qwen models persistent and initial_only arms already exist in results/response_v3 with identical prompts/seeds; only anchor25, anchor50, in_history are run.
stopping: Fixed sample counts; no outcome-dependent stopping or condition replacement.
dose_amendment: 2026-11-15 16:40: added dose variants (1 and 6 seeds vs base 3) sharing base graph/task/exposure/sampling seeds; paired with the base schedule control. Added after v3 analysis showed perturbation memory; ABM dose predictions frozen before these runs.
memory_amendment: 2026-11-15 23:20: added init_fullmem (memory ablation) to test whether persistence requires the 1-step memory constraint. Same Spec/block_id/sampling seeds as initial_only; only the prompt's own-history window changes.
